headline: Three Small-Caps, One Optical Boom, and a Chatbot's Verdict
lede: A retail investor on X reports that Google's reasoning model, asked to compare a soaring Swedish photonics stock against two of his other holdings, declined to anoint the obvious winner. The episode is a tidy snapshot of a real industry shift, the speculative froth around it, and the limits of asking a language model to do the work of a portfolio manager.
body:
The post comes from @napoleon21st, an account whose substantive footprint outside X is faint enough that little can be said about its track record. The argument, however, is concrete: Sivers Semiconductors ($SIVE on Nasdaq Stockholm) is on a generational tear, yet a Gemini Pro 'thinking model' (Google's reasoning-tuned variant, designed to plan before it answers) preferred two more obscure names, Silicom ($SILC, NASDAQ) and LPKF Laser & Electronics ($LPK, XETRA).

The Sivers run is real. The shares closed near SEK 56 on 5 May 2026, up roughly 1,250% year-to-date and around 800% in three months, valuing the company near nine billion kronor. The catalyst is a tangible product story: Sivers makes indium phosphide (InP) distributed feedback lasers, the small light-emitting chips that sit at the heart of optical transceivers in AI data centres. In April it announced a collaboration with the contract manufacturer Jabil on a 1.6 terabit-per-second linear-drive optical module, and a separate LiDAR customer is on track to ramp in late 2026 with cumulative lifetime revenue Sivers itself pegs at $53m-$138m. That is not nothing for a company doing roughly SEK 304m in 2025 sales. It is also, as the OCR text in the bookmark concedes, a balance-sheet story with a hole in it: 2025 produced an after-tax loss of SEK 186m, and a directed share issue at SEK 14.50 in April raised SEK 125m, with management estimating dilution of about 2.5% on a fully-diluted basis. The model's caveat about 'ongoing dilution risks' is fair; the bigger risk is that the stock now prices in execution that has not yet happened.

Silicom is the un-glamorous comparison. The Israeli maker of network interface cards and edge appliances posted Q1 2026 revenue of $19.1m, up 33% year-over-year, guided full-year revenue to $82-83m, and finished the quarter with $63m in cash and equivalents, $63m in inventory and no debt. Management has secured four design wins in the first four months against an annual target of seven to nine, with proof-of-concept inference deployments at tier-one hyperscalers slated for the second half of 2026. The bookmark's quote that SILC trades 'at its cash value' overstates the case: cash and securities of about $109m sit inside a market capitalisation considerably larger than that. But the spirit is right. SILC is a profitable, growing, asset-light business changing hands at roughly six times normalised earnings.

LPKF is the most heterodox of the three. The Garbsen-based company sells laser systems, and its proprietary LIDE process (Laser-Induced Deep Etching, a method for creating high-density holes in thin glass) is being marketed as the enabling step for glass interposers and glass core substrates in advanced semiconductor packaging, including co-packaged optics, or CPO, the architecture that bonds optical engines directly onto switch silicon to cut power and latency. Both Nvidia (Quantum-X, Spectrum-X) and Broadcom (Tomahawk 6 'Davisson') are bringing CPO platforms to market in 2026. LPKF guides 2026 group revenue of EUR 105-120m at an adjusted EBIT margin between -3% and 4.5%, with semiconductor ramp orders expected in 2027-28. The shares have moved accordingly, recently around EUR 20 against a 52-week low of EUR 5.35.

The meta-question is whether Gemini's preference for SILC and LPK over a parabolic SIVE deserves any weight. Recent academic work suggests scepticism. A 2025 arXiv paper, 'Your AI, Not Your View,' shows that frontier LLMs hold persistent directional biases on individual stocks that survive counter-evidence; another (Koa et al., 2025) finds that previously reported LLM stock-picking edges largely vanish under longer windows and broader cross-sections, with survivorship and data-snooping biases inflating headline results. A reasoning model comparing three tickers is, in effect, stitching together training-data sentiment and recent prompt context; it is not running a discounted cash-flow model. The poster's own framing - 'It's not necessarily true but it shows how strong these other picks are' - smuggles in the inference that a chatbot's relative ranking is evidence of underlying quality. It is evidence, mostly, that the chatbot has read the same bull theses he has.

concepts.definition: A chip-packaging architecture that places the optical transceiver - the component that converts electrical signals into light for fibre transmission - directly alongside the switch ASIC, eliminating the pluggable module and its digital signal processor. The motivation is power: at the bandwidths AI clusters now demand, traditional pluggable optics consume too many watts per bit. Both Nvidia and Broadcom have CPO platforms reaching customers in 2026.

A semiconductor laser built on indium phosphide rather than silicon, with a 'distributed feedback' grating that locks emission to a single, stable wavelength. InP DFBs are the workhorse light source for high-speed data-centre optical links because silicon, by itself, cannot efficiently emit light. Sivers is one of a small number of independent suppliers.

LPKF's patented process for drilling and structuring thin glass at high density and precision, used to make glass interposers - flat substrates with vertical metal-filled vias that connect chiplets. Glass is being adopted as a packaging substrate because it is flatter and more dimensionally stable than the organic laminates currently in use, and is increasingly relevant to advanced packaging and CPO.

The reduction in each existing shareholder's ownership percentage when a company issues new equity. For unprofitable growth companies, repeated capital raises are routine and necessary; the question is whether the new cash funds revenue that grows faster than the share count. Sivers' April 2026 SEK 125m raise was small (about 2.5% dilution), but the long-running cadence of issuances is a recurring concern.

A class of large language model fine-tuned to produce an extended internal chain of reasoning before answering, exemplified by Google's Gemini Pro thinking variants and OpenAI's o-series. Useful for multi-step problems, but susceptible to the same training-data biases as ordinary LLMs - and prone, in financial contexts, to overconfident conclusions even when the underlying data is thin.

fact_check: The post itself contains no falsifiable factual claims beyond the model's reported output, so there is little to refute directly. The OCR'd LLM text it shares is rougher. Calling SILC a play on buying 'a company at its cash value' is loose: cash and securities of roughly $109m sit inside a market cap meaningfully larger than that, though the company is debt-free with revenue compounding in the low-30s percent. The OCR text's '33%' growth figure for SILC matches the Q1 2026 print. The claim that LPKF will deliver a structural 10x rests on a semiconductor ramp the company itself flags for 2027-28, not 2026; LPKF's own 2026 guidance allows for an EBIT margin as low as -3%. None of these are errors by the poster, who is quoting a model output and labelling it as such, but readers should not mistake the model's confidence for due diligence.
